subject: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@pinebrookbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. I pulled together a short proposal for the evidence walkthrough your SOC/CSA team asked for. Key items we can cover in the 30–45 minute session:

- Mapping of our CAIQ responses to runtime telemetry and key control artifacts (how requests map to logs)
- Timestamping and retention windows for per-tenant telemetry, KV cache traces, and prefix/cache hits
- How we produce sampled extraction packages (what we can provide without exposing tenant data)
- Ownership and signoffs for control assertions (who signs the attestation)

I attached a draft control list (Pinebrook_CSA_Control_List.xlsx) with the rows I think are most relevant. Before I finalize the walkthrough deck, two clarifying asks: (1) For retention clarifications — do you need raw per-request logs or are aggregated, timestamped traces sufficient for your reviewers? (2) Any constraints on redaction (e.g., remove prompt text) we should prepare for?

Proposed times (all ET): 8/17 11:00–11:45, 8/17 15:00–15:45, or 8/18 10:00–10:45. Which works best?

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Pinebrook_CSA_Control_List.xlsx
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@pinebrookbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: security@pinebrookbank.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications

Michael —

Thanks — 8/17 15:00 ET is best for our security reviewers.

To answer your questions up front:
- Our auditors will accept aggregated, timestamped traces for high-volume endpoints, but they want raw per-request traces (with PII redacted) for any controls tied to tenant isolation and keying.
- Redaction: remove prompt content and any user-provided PII. We expect preserved request/response metadata (request_id, model_id, timestamp, route) and the KV-cache hit/miss indicators.
- Please include evidence that shows retention windows are enforced (policy + proof), and an example extraction that demonstrates how we would remove prompt text while keeping operational fields.

I'll loop in our compliance lead on the call — cc'd security@pinebrookbank.com. See you 8/17 15:00 ET.

Best,
Elena Cruz
Lead, Third-Party Risk & Cloud Security
Pinebrook Bank
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@pinebrookbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications

Elena —

Great, 8/17 15:00 ET confirmed. We'll prepare two extraction artifacts for the call:

1) Aggregated telemetry bundle (suitable for high-volume endpoints) — includes timestamped token counts, latency percentiles, route IDs, and batching cadence.
2) Sample per-request trace (redacted) — request_id, model_variant, timestamp, kv_cache_hit boolean, prefix_cache_key (hashed), and response metadata. Prompt/response text will be removed.

Naomi — can you pull a recent runtime-telemetry-sample.log and the kv-cache-timestamps.csv (hashed keys) for the demo? We should remove any raw prompt content but preserve the request_id/timestamps chain so Pinebrook's auditors can verify continuity.

Kimberly — I'll include the policy excerpt that demonstrates retention windows and the automated retention job that expires telemetry after the configured window. Also planning to show our sampling/offset logic so auditors see we don't leak prompt text in bulk bundles.

Attachment: runtime-telemetry-sample.log (will upload before the meeting).

Michael
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 13:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications

On it — pulling examples now. Quick notes for the demo artifacts:

- runtime-telemetry-sample.log will contain event lines with ISO8601 timestamps and a request_id; content fields redacted. I will also include a short README to explain which fields are redacted and how to verify integrity (HMAC of the timestamp chain).
- kv-cache-timestamps.csv will include hashed cache keys, hit/miss flags, and an event timestamp column. We will show a short script that walks the chain from a request_id to the kv-cache events (no secret material included).
- For retention proof, Kimberley, can you confirm the job name and the S3 lifecycle rule ID we reference in the policy? I have the sample logs ready but will only upload the zip to the secure Drive link when Michael says so.

Naomi
Principal Systems Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@pinebrookbank.com>, security@pinebrookbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook CSA: evidence walkthrough and retention clarifications

Elena —

Thanks, all set. Naomi will upload the artifact bundle to the Drive link below by EOD Monday 8/16; bundle will include: runtime-telemetry-sample.log, kv-cache-timestamps.csv, README.md (redaction notes), and a short retention-policy-excerpt.pdf.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-pinebrook-csa

On the call we'll walk through: control mapping -> artifact provenance (how timestamps map to control assertions) -> sample redaction run -> where to find the automated retention job in the console. Expected duration 35 minutes with 10 minutes Q&A.

If Pinebrook security needs an NDA or DocuSign for the artifact transfer, please send the link and we'll get it executed before upload.

Looking forward to it — Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments uploaded: runtime-telemetry-sample.log, kv-cache-timestamps.csv
